supporting_observations.claim: The evidence contains one failed logon for eli.brooks at 13:44:02, using LogonType 2 on WS-EBROOKS-01; the status and substatus indicate an incorrect password.
About 82 seconds before that failure, eli.brooks had a successful interactive logon on the same workstation, followed by a normal userinit.exe and explorer.exe session startup.

The available records show ordinary user-session activity after the failed attempt, including Firefox opening Zoom and browsing Microsoft 365 and Bing; this is consistent with continued workstation use, though it does not prove who was at the device.

The supplied evidence does not show repeated failed logons: it contains one 4625 record in the requested window. Taken together with the preceding successful interactive session, the failure is more consistent with an isolated incorrect-password entry than demonstrated malicious activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: Only one failed-logon record is present in the supplied evidence, so the alert's claim of repeated failures cannot be verified from these records.
No domain-controller authentication records or other failed-logon events for eli.brooks are included in the supplied evidence.
The logs do not identify who entered the incorrect password or establish the user's intent.
claims_not_established: That the failure was definitely a user typo or credential re-entry.
That additional failed attempts did not occur outside the supplied records.
That the successful logon and subsequent activity were performed by eli.brooks personally.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: Google Drive File Stream ran under eli.brooks's account, and the workstation accessed drive.google.com. Google Drive is not among the approved storage services listed in the environment context. This is outside the alerted authentication activity and does not determine this disposition. (T191-00016, T191-00103, T191-00104)
